question.value: What are the spatially-resolved sizes, morphologies, molecular gas masses, and kinematics of 11 dusty star-forming galaxies at z~2 in the GOODS-S field, and how do dusty, gaseous, and stellar components and AGN activity drive their evolution?

evidence.quote: We include galaxy multi-band images and photometry (in the optical, radio and X-rays) to investigate the interlink between dusty, gaseous and stellar components and the eventual presence of AGN.

claims.hypothesis: In the in-situ galaxy-BH co-evolution scenario (Lapi et al. 2018), high-z star-forming progenitors of ETGs undergo gas compaction, resulting in compact dust-obscured star formation at radii <= R_rot (~1 kpc), more extended mildly-obscured optical stellar emission out to R_Q (~a few kpc), and inflowing rotating molecular gas traced by CO at intermediate/larger scales than the dust.
claims.experiment: Measured circularized physical radii of ALMA dust continuum (via 2D Gaussian fits in CASA imfit) and CO emission for 11 z~2 DSFGs in GOODS-S, and compared them with HST/WFC3 H160 optical radii and the theoretical size-mass relation.
claims.result: Six of 11 sources are resolved in ALMA continuum with median r_ALMA = 1.15 kpc (all < 5 kpc), median r_H / r_ALMA = 2.05 (always > 1), and median r_CO = 3.45 kpc (r_CO / r_ALMA = 2.2, r_H / r_CO = 1.7).
claims.finding: The observed multi-band size hierarchy (r_ALMA < r_CO <= r_H) and compact FIR sizes agree with the gas compaction phase predicted by the in-situ galaxy evolution scenario.

evidence.quote: This trend is present in all the six sources of our sample that are resolved both in the HST H$_{160}$ (optical sizes; filled squares in Fig. [4](#fig:sizes)) and ALMA continuum maps (millimeter sizes; filled stars in Fig. [4](#fig:sizes))

This is consistent with the size evolution scenario presented in (cite: Lapi2018a:2018ApJ...857...22L) according to which the CO emission traces the rotating cold gas phase that, while inflowing towards the central regions of the galaxy, fuels both the mildly-obscured star formation at larger radii (traced by the emission in the optical) and the highly-obscured star formation in the innermost regions (sampled by the dust continuum in the (sub-)millimeter).

claims.hypothesis: CO J>1 spectral line kinematics in these z~2 DSFGs trace rotating molecular gas discs and/or forthcoming/ongoing AGN-driven molecular outflows.
claims.experiment: Extracted 1D CO spectra, Gaussian line fits, moment 0, 1, and 2 maps for UDF1, UDF3, UDF8, and ALESS067.1, and a position-velocity diagram for ALESS067.1 from archival ALMA cubes.
claims.result: UDF3, UDF8, and ALESS067.1 show asymmetric double-peaked CO profiles (broad component FWHM < 400 km/s) and velocity gradients; UDF1 shows a narrow single-peaked profile (FWHM ~ 170 km/s); ALESS067.1 shows a mom2 central peak with a tail and an asymmetric pv diagram.
claims.finding: The CO lines reveal rotating discs of molecular gas (face-on for UDF1), while features in UDF3, UDF8, and ALESS067.1 are also suggestive of AGN-driven molecular outflows or interactions, though higher spatial and spectral resolution is needed to disentangle the scenarios.

evidence.quote: CO lines reveal the presence of a rotating disc of molecular gas, but we can not exclude either the presence of interactions and/or molecular outflows. Images at higher (spectral and spatial) resolution are needed to disentangle from the possible scenarios.
The double-peaked spectral line profile of three CO lines, along with their velocity and velocity dispersion maps, are consistent with both a rotating disc of molecular gas and an AGN outflow.

claims.hypothesis: Differences between molecular gas masses inferred from dust continuum and from low-J CO lines arise because CO and dust emission trace different spatial scales and optical depths.
claims.experiment: Derived M_H2 from CO(3-2) and CO(2-1) luminosities for UDF1, UDF3, UDF8, and ALESS067.1 assuming Daddi et al. (2015) excitation and alpha_CO = 3.6, and compared with dust-continuum gas masses and measured r_CO / r_ALMA ratios.
claims.result: CO-derived gas masses (e.g., 15x10^10 M_sun for UDF3, 5.8x10^10 M_sun for UDF8, 16.8x10^10 M_sun for ALESS067.1) exceed dust-derived gas masses (4, 1.0, and 8 x 10^10 M_sun respectively), while r_CO is typically larger than r_ALMA (median r_CO / r_ALMA = 2.2).
claims.finding: Differences in molecular gas mass estimates and depletion timescales between dust continuum and CO lines are traced back to CO emission being more spatially extended than dust continuum and optically thick.

evidence.quote: We identified some differences in the molecular gas masses estimated by using the dust optically-thin continuum and CO lines, that obviously imply diverse depletion timescales $\tau_\star$ (cf. Tab. [\[tab:summary_integral\]](#tab:summary_integral) and Tab. [\[tab:summary_resolved\]](#tab:summary_resolved)).
These differences can be traced back to diverse dust and CO sizes, the latter being typically larger than the former and its emission almost optically thick (especially in case of low-J CO lines).

why_this_data.value: Selected public ALMA archival maps with the highest spatial resolution (<= 1 arcsec) in Bands 6, 7, and 9 for a homogeneous sample of 11 spectroscopically confirmed z~2 DSFGs in GOODS-S that already have complete X-ray-to-radio SED modelling.

evidence.quote: We analyse the public ALMA archival maps containing our 11 DSFGs and we select the ones that have the best spatial resolution ($\Delta\theta\lesssim1$ arcsec) in the wavelength range $\lambda_{\rm obs}\sim 500\mu$m $-$ 3 mm (corresponding to the frequency range $\nu_{\rm obs}\sim 100-600$ GHz).
Almost all of the best spatially-resolved continuum maps are in ALMA B6 and B7 that, indeed, constitute a very good compromise between spatial resolution and the sampled wavelength.

why_this_method.value: Used image-plane 2D Gaussian fitting (CASA imfit) because visibility-domain fitting was precluded by the noise level; preferred CO-derived gas masses over dust-continuum gas masses because dust continuum can miss gas at larger radii; rebinned spectral channels to reduce noise and boost CO line signal.

evidence.quote: The level of noise did not allow us to extract the sizes from a fit in the visibility domains.

Images native spectral resolution in most cases was too small to allow the CO line profile to be clearly detected. In such cases we perform a rebin (using the CASA task *imrebin*[^2]) of the line channels.

While characterizing galaxy cold gas phase we preferentially use the gas mass measurements from CO spectral lines (when available; see Tab. [\[tab:summary_resolved\]](#tab:summary_resolved)) rather than the ones from dust continuum (Tab. [\[tab:summary_integral\]](#tab:summary_integral)), since the latter can miss the gas distributed over scales larger than the dust continuum size

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Extracting continuum source sizes from a fit in the visibility (uv) domain was considered, but rejected because the noise level did not allow it.

evidence.quote: The level of noise did not allow us to extract the sizes from a fit in the visibility domains.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: 3D tilted-ring kinematic modelling of CO(3-2) with 3D-Barolo was considered for ALESS067.1, but not performed due to insufficient spatial and spectral resolution in the ALMA cube.

evidence.quote: A clear interpretation requires higher spectral and spatial resolution in the ALMA cube, that would have allowed to model the CO(3-2) kinematics, exploiting e.g., 3D-Barolo (cite: DiTeodoro&Fraternali2015:2015MNRAS.451.3021D)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Alternative CO conversion factor alpha_CO = 1.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 (often preferred for compact SMGs) was considered alongside alpha_CO = 3.6; authors provide a 0.5 rescaling factor rather than favouring one.

evidence.quote: However, due to the large uncertainties on $\alpha_{\rm CO}$, we do not favour one or the other value and we suggest just to re-scale the resulting molecular gas in Tab. [1](#tab:CO_gas_mol) by a factor $1.8/3.6=0.5$.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Selected the highest spatial resolution archival maps currently available and emphasized that higher spatial and spectral resolution observations are still needed to disentangle rotating discs from outflows and interactions.

evidence.quote: Images at higher (spectral and spatial) resolution are needed to disentangle from the possible scenarios.

Finally, we stress the need of more sensitive multi-wavelength maps and higher spatial and spectral resolution images in the diverse spectral bands to definitely clarify the relative impact of in-situ processes, galaxy interactions and AGN feedback

limitations_admitted.value: 5 out of 11 sources in continuum maps (listed as 6 out of 11 in text, 5 marked with sb in Table 2) and all 4 CO-detected sources in mom0 maps are unresolved by 2D Gaussian fitting, yielding only upper limits or peak-separation estimates.

evidence.quote: Some of the detections (6 out of 11) are not resolved in the corresponding ALMA map: in such a case we indicate the synthesized beam size (labelled with the apex *sb*) that provides an upper limit on the source size.

Since they all appear unresolved to a 2D Gaussian fit, we provide: an upper limit on UDF1 CO emission size, given by the synthesized beam; a measure of UDF3, UDF8 and ALESS067.1 CO emission equal to the angular distance between the peaks of the two spectral line components.

limitations_admitted.value: Current spatial and spectral resolution of the CO data cubes is insufficient to definitively disentangle rotating molecular gas discs from AGN-driven outflows or galaxy interactions.

evidence.quote: CO lines reveal the presence of a rotating disc of molecular gas, but we can not exclude either the presence of interactions and/or molecular outflows. Images at higher (spectral and spatial) resolution are needed to disentangle from the possible scenarios.

limitations_admitted.value: Large uncertainty in the CO-to-H2 conversion factor alpha_CO and assumed CO excitation ladder.

evidence.quote: However, due to the large uncertainties on $\alpha_{\rm CO}$, we do not favour one or the other value and we suggest just to re-scale the resulting molecular gas in Tab. [1](#tab:CO_gas_mol) by a factor $1.8/3.6=0.5$.

limitations_admitted.value: Sensitivity limits and low spatial resolution in the ALESS067.1 CO(6-5) map may miss extended CO emission and prevent spatial comparison with CO(3-2).

evidence.quote: The low spatial resolution of the image does not allow to spatially compare the size of the two spectral emission, neither to understand the origin of the $J=6$ line

The sightly lower value we find is probably due to sensitivity limit that makes us miss the outskirts of the CO emission, coupled with low resolution that causes the flux to be distributed on a larger image area

referee_caveats_inferred: Some flux density values and bands in the Appendix text conflict with Table 2 (e.g., AzTEC.GS21 is listed in Table 2 as B6 with 954+-74 uJy, but Appendix 7.10 states a B9 flux of 12+-1 mJy in Table 2; AzTEC.GS22 is 6400+-880 uJy in Table 2 but 5.8+-0.8 mJy in Appendix 7.11).

CO sizes for UDF3, UDF8, and ALESS067.1 are estimated from the angular separation between double-peaked spectral components rather than deconvolved profile fits, which may systematically bias r_CO compared to Gaussian half-light radii.
Heterogeneous archival continuum bands (B6, B7, B9) and angular resolutions (0.08 to 0.62 arcsec) across the 11 galaxies may introduce resolution/wavelength biases in the median r_ALMA.
Table 1 has an unlabelled column between z and AGN where AGN symbols were lost in formatting.
